Model evidence: Consistently prominent: full-cohort permutation ranks 2/2/1 and XGBoost SHAP rank 1; remains highly prominent after early ANC is added.
Observed pathway pattern: Large wealth differences appear at ANC entry, progression to ANC4+, early initiation, and ANC8+ attainment. Among early initiators, ANC8+ was 19.1% in the poorest quintile versus 62.4% in the richest.
Programme-review question: Which barriers affecting poorer women remain after they enter ANC and even when initiation is timely?
Additional evidence needed: Local information on direct and indirect costs, transport, service availability, appointment continuity, outreach and financial-access arrangements.

Model evidence: Full-cohort SHAP rank 2 and XGBoost permutation rank 3; remains among the leading predictors after early ANC is added.
Observed pathway pattern: Longer travel is associated with lower ANC entry, lower progression to ANC4+, and lower ANC8+ attainment. Even among early initiators, ANC8+ declined from 48.2% at 0–30 minutes to 18.5% at >120 minutes.
Programme-review question: Where does repeated travel burden interfere with timely entry and sustained ANC attendance?
Additional evidence needed: Facility catchment geography, service distribution, outreach coverage, transport availability, referral arrangements and local travel-cost information.

Model evidence: Highly consistent across algorithms: full-cohort permutation ranks 1/1/2 and SHAP rank 3; extended-model permutation ranks 2/2/2.
Observed pathway pattern: Regional patterns differ by pathway stage. Somali shows a large ANC-entry deficit; Central Ethiopia and Tigray show stronger entry but weaker later continuation; Afar shows lower entry but comparatively stronger continuation among women progressing through ANC.
Programme-review question: At which ANC stage does each regional gap emerge, and what local service or population context corresponds to that stage?
Additional evidence needed: Regional and woreda routine-service data, facility readiness, service organisation, workforce, outreach, access conditions and programme implementation information.

Model evidence: Ranked first by permutation importance in all three extended models and first by extended XGBoost SHAP. Incremental performance point estimates improved, but all paired confidence intervals included zero.
Observed pathway pattern: ANC8+ was 42.4% among early initiators versus 11.1% among later initiators. However, 57.6% of early initiators still did not reach ANC8+.
Programme-review question: How can programmes distinguish barriers to timely initiation from barriers to continuity after timely initiation?
Additional evidence needed: First-contact processes, pregnancy identification, scheduling, return-visit systems, appointment adherence and continuity-of-care information.

Model evidence: More prominent in the ANC-entry extended models: permutation ranks 5/3/5 and XGBoost SHAP rank 5.
Observed pathway pattern: Occupation groups show different pathway profiles rather than a simple ordered gradient. Professional/clerical women show high entry and early initiation, while differences among other groups change across later ANC stages.
Programme-review question: Do work conditions, time availability, livelihood patterns or service schedules contribute to different ANC attendance pathways?
Additional evidence needed: Local work schedules, seasonal livelihood patterns, clinic hours, waiting time, opportunity costs and qualitative evidence from women.

Model evidence: Consistently prominent in the full-cohort models with permutation ranks 3/3/4 and XGBoost SHAP rank 4; remains prominent in the extended ANC-entry model.
Observed pathway pattern: Religion-group differences occur at entry, timing and later attainment. For example, Protestant women had near-national ANC entry but lower early initiation and lower ANC8+ after ANC4+. Patterns differ from those observed among Muslim women.
Programme-review question: What geographic, social, community or service-context factors underlie these observed group differences?
Additional evidence needed: Region, residence and service-context information plus locally appropriate qualitative evidence. Religion itself should not be treated as the causal mechanism.

Model evidence: Prominent particularly in XGBoost/SHAP, but less consistent across algorithms than the leading predictors.
Observed pathway pattern: ANC entry was lower among women reporting the pregnancy was wanted no more, while progression to ANC4+ was lower among both 'wanted later' and 'wanted no more' groups than among women reporting 'wanted then'.
Programme-review question: Does reproductive context identify women who need additional support to remain engaged with ANC after entry?
Additional evidence needed: Family-planning and pregnancy-intention context, counselling pathways, social support and qualitative evidence. Retrospective intention reporting should be interpreted cautiously.
